A Dictionary of Urdu, Classical Hindi, and English. A Dictionary of Urdu, Classical Hindi, and English. Search for headword: 'sakāl' 8 results Highlight text and press "t" to transliterate (devanagari script only) 1) ساکليه sākalya
                        ( p. 626 ) S ساکليه साकल्य sākalya (fr. sakala ), s.m. Totality, entireness, completeness; the whole, all. 2) سکالنا sakālnā
                        ( p. 663 ) H سکالنا सकालना sakālnā , v.t. = sakārnā , q.v. 3) سکالي sakālī
                        ( p. 663 ) H سکالي सकाली sakālī [S. सकाल + इका ], s.f. Early morning, dawn ( = sakāl ); — adv. Early in the morning ( = sakāle ). 4) سکل sakal
                        ( p. 664 ) S سکل सकल sakal , adj. All, entire, the whole, every, each and all: — sakal-ur-bāsī , s.m. lit. 'Dwelling in all hearts'; an epithet of Vishnu. 5) شاکل śākal
                        ( p. 718 ) S شاکل शाकल śākal , s.m. Name of a school of the Rig-veda (supposed to have been founded by the elder Śākalya); — s.f. A mixture of sesasum seeds, barley, ghī , coarse sugar, fruits, &c., used by Hindūs in oblations to the gods. 6) شاکلا śākalā
                        ( p. 718 ) H شاکلا शाकला śākalā , s.f. = śākal , q.v. 7) شاکلا śākalā
                        ( p. 718 ) H شاکلا शाकला śākalā [S. शाकलास् ], s.m. pl. Name of a tribe inhabiting Bhārat-varsha; the followers of the Śākala school of the Veda. 8) شاکليه śākalya
                        ( p. 718 ) H شاکليه शाकल्य śākalya , corr. of sākalya , q.v. Search Form • DDSA Close

A Dictionary of Urdu, Classical Hindi, and English. A Dictionary of Urdu, Classical Hindi, and English. Search for headword: 'sakār' 14 results Highlight text and press "t" to transliterate (devanagari script only) 1) ساکار sākār
                        ( p. 625 ) S ساکار साकार sākār ( sa + ākāra ), adj. Possessed of form or shape, of definite figure, figurate. 2) سکار sakār
                        ( p. 663 ) H سکار सकार sakār , s.m. = sa-kāl , q.v. 3) سکار sakār
                        ( p. 663 ) H سکار सकार sakār [S. स्वीकारः ], s.m. Acceptance (of a hunḍī or bill), endorsement (of a bill) noting acceptance. 4) سکارا sakārā
                        ( p. 663 ) H سکارا सकारा sakārā , s.m. = H سکارائی सकाराई sakārāʼī , s.f. [S. स्वीकार + कः and इका ], Charge for accepting and cashing (a bill of exchange). 5) سکارائی sakārāʼī
                        ( p. 663 ) H سکارائی सकाराई sakārāʼī , s.f. = H سکارا सकारा sakārā , s.m. [S. स्वीकार + कः and इका ], Charge for accepting and cashing (a bill of exchange). 6) سکارن sakāraṇ
                        ( p. 663 ) S سکارن सकारण sakāraṇ , adj. Having some cause, originating from a cause. 7) سکارنا sakārnā
                        ( p. 663 ) H سکارنا सकारना sakārnā (fr. sakār ), v.t. To accept, or endorse as accepted (a bill): — sakārne-wālā , s.m. Accepter, or endorser (of a bill): — sakāre-pīćhe bećnā or bećī karnā , To negotiate (a bill) after acceptance. 8) سکاري sakārī
                        ( p. 663 ) H سکاري सकारी sakārī , s.f. = sakālī or sa-kāl ; — adv. = sakāle ; qq.v. 9) سکاري sakāre
                        ( p. 663 ) H سکاري सकारे sakāre , adv. = sakāle , q.v. 10) سکرات sakarāt, sakrāt
                        ( p. 664 ) A سکرات sakarāt , sakrāt (pl. of sakrat , v.n. fr. سکر ; see sukr ), s.f. Fainting, insensibility, agony (of death): — sakarāt-ě-maut , s.f. Insensibility attendant upon death, pangs or agony of death. 11) سکڙ sakaṛ
                        ( p. 664 ) H سکڙ सकड़ sakaṛ , adj. = sakal , q.v. 12) سکڙدادا sakaṛ-dādā
                        ( p. 664 ) H سکڙدادا सकड़दादा sakaṛ-dādā (prob. sakal + dādā , qq.v.), s.m. Great-grandfather, or great-great-grandfather (on the father's side). 13) سکڙنا sakaṛnā, sukaṛnā, sikuṛnā, sikaṛnā
                        ( p. 664 ) H سکڙنا सकड़ना sakaṛnā , सुकड़ना sukaṛnā , सिकुड़ना sikuṛnā , सिकड़ना sikaṛnā [ sakaṛ˚ , &c. = Prk. संकड्ढ ( इ ), fr. संकड्ढ = S. सङ्क्टष्ट p.p.p. of rt. सम् + कृष् ], v.n. To draw together, draw in or up, to become contracted, to contract, to become tightened or tight; to dwindle; to shrink, shrivel, to curl up, to wrinkle; to be gathered together, be collected, to gather, collect; to be swept up or together: — sikuṛ-jānā , or sikaṛ-jānā , &c. v.n. Intens. of and = sikuṛnā . 14) سکڙنانا sakaṛ-nānā
                        ( p. 664 ) H سکڙنانا सकड़नाना sakaṛ-nānā (prob. sakal + nānā ), s.m. Great-grandfather, or great-great-grandfather (on the mother's side). Search Form • DDSA Close

                        ( p. 193 ) H بهنسار भिनसार bhinsār (for bihan-sār , from bihān , q.v.), s.m. Dawn of day, day-break, day-light, early morning (also written bhinusār , bhinnsār ); — adv. At dawn, &c. Search Form • DDSA Close
